Below is a small character-level language model: a 4-layer transformer with 6 attention heads per layer, which reads up to 128 characters and outputs scores (logits) for the next character. This is exactly how it computes (numpy): ```python import numpy as np VOCAB = "\n " + "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" # index 0 = newline, 1 = space, 2..27 = a..z HEADS, LAYERS = 6, 4 def layer_norm(x, w, b): # over the last axis, eps 1e-5 mu = x.mean(-1, keepdims=True) var = ((x - mu) ** 2).mean(-1, keepdims=True) return (x - mu) / np.sqrt(var + 1e-5) * w + b def next_char_logits(text, p): """text: up to 128 characters (only the last 128 are used); p: dict of the weight arrays. Returns the 28 logits for the character that comes next.""" ids = [VOCAB.index(c) for c in text[-128:]] n, d = len(ids), p["tok_emb"].shape[1] hd = d // HEADS x = p["tok_emb"][ids] + p["pos_emb"][:n] # (n, d); positions 0..n-1 from the start of the text for l in range(LAYERS): # layer l uses the tensors named . h = layer_norm(x, p[f"ln1_w.{l}"], p[f"ln1_b.{l}"]) q, k, v = h @ p[f"W_q.{l}"].T, h @ p[f"W_k.{l}"].T, h @ p[f"W_v.{l}"].T out = np.zeros((n, d)) for j in range(HEADS): # head j uses dimensions j*hd .. (j+1)*hd - 1 s = slice(j * hd, (j + 1) * hd) att = q[:, s] @ k[:, s].T / np.sqrt(hd) # (n, n) att = att + np.triu(np.full((n, n), -np.inf), 1) # causal: position i sees positions 0..i att = np.exp(att - att.max(-1, keepdims=True)) att = att / att.sum(-1, keepdims=True) out[:, s] = att @ v[:, s] x = x + out @ p[f"W_o.{l}"].T h = layer_norm(x, p[f"ln2_w.{l}"], p[f"ln2_b.{l}"]) x = x + np.maximum(0.0, h @ p[f"W_fc.{l}"].T) @ p[f"W_proj.{l}"].T # ReLU MLP, hidden 4 d h = layer_norm(x, p["lnf_w"], p["lnf_b"]) return h[-1] @ p["W_out"].T + p["b_out"] # logits of the next character (28) ``` Training: from random initialization (every matrix entry drawn from a normal distribution with standard deviation 0.02, or 0.007071 for W_o and W_proj; LayerNorm weights 1 and biases 0; b_out 0), next-character prediction with AdamW (30,517 steps of 256 random 128-character windows, 1,000,000,000 characters in total; learning-rate warm-up then cosine decay; weight decay 0.01 on the matrices). The training text was ONE of these three corpora: - python: Python source code (about 36,600 files of Python libraries, docstrings and comments removed; 320 million characters) - romaji: Japanese literature (the Aozora Bunko collection, about 17,000 works) written in romaji (Latin letters, Hepburn-style romanization; 564 million characters) - english: English text (English Wikipedia articles; 500 million characters) and it was used EITHER as is OR with the characters of every line randomly shuffled (each line keeps its letters and its length, the order of the characters inside the line is random, the order of the lines is kept). Normalization (the same for all three corpora, before anything else): lowercased; in each line the leading spaces (indentation) were kept, every other character that is not a letter a-z became a space, runs of spaces were collapsed to one and trailing spaces removed. So the text contains only newlines, spaces and the letters a-z (the 28 characters of VOCAB). WHAT YOU CAN USE. The weights inside the four transformer blocks, exactly as trained (float32): for layer l = 0, 1, 2 and 3, ln1_w.l, ln1_b.l, W_q.l, W_k.l, W_v.l, W_o.l (attention) and ln2_w.l, ln2_b.l, W_fc.l, W_proj.l (MLP). The input layer (tok_emb, the 28 x d character embeddings, and pos_emb, the 128 x d position embeddings) and the output layer (lnf_w, lnf_b, W_out, b_out) are NOT available. The d = 384 dimensions of the residual stream carry no labels. Head j of layer l uses rows 64j .. 64j+63 of W_q.l, W_k.l and W_v.l and columns 64j .. 64j+63 of W_o.l.
